boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 52 features, measured 2026-11-11. It is the map the sitting members were elected from in 2024. California's voters adopted a new map in November 2025 (Proposition 50) and the November 2026 election used it (TIGERweb layer 0); 44 of the 52 districts differ between the two, so the app switches maps on 3 January 2027, when the members elected from the new one take their seats. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: Members come from the unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset, refreshed weekly and reviewed before it ships.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET OUTSIDE SAN FRANCISCO. State law gives every California county a board of five supervisors, and each county elects officers such as a sheriff, a district attorney and an assessor; no list of them was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. San Francisco is a city and county whose 11 supervisors the Supervisor District card names. Recorded as gap ca-county-officials.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside California, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside California (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='06'.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: California. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 483 incorporated cities and towns, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or town containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 483 features for California, measured 2026-11-11: 462 cities and 21 towns, all active governments. MOST OF CALIFORNIA'S LAND IS IN NO CITY OR TOWN (5.4% of it, 21,635.6 of 403,676.5 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of California's mayors and council members was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. San Francisco's Board of Supervisors is named on the Supervisor District card. Recorded as gap ca-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — California has 150 pieces, 103 reservations and rancherias and 47 pieces of off-reservation trust land, held by 98 nations, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py on 2026-11-12, with the counties measured against this app's own county outlines. The largest are the Hoopa Valley Reservation (366.8 km², Humboldt County), the Yurok Reservation (226.5 km², Humboldt and Del Norte counties), the Tule River Reservation (218.1 km², Tulare County), the Colorado River Indian Reservation (195.1 km² in California, 16.2% of it, San Bernardino and Riverside counties) and the Fort Yuma Indian Reservation (172.6 km², 95.4% of it, Imperial County); the smallest is the Likely Rancheria (0.006 km², Modoc County). Five pieces cross the state line and are drawn whole: the Colorado River, Fort Mojave (18.5% in California), Fort Yuma and Timbi-Sha Shoshone (21.9%) reservations and the Washoe Ranches Trust Land (0.3%). The Colorado River Indian Tribes are seated in Arizona and the Washoe Tribe in Nevada. The Census draws tribal districts on the Yurok Reservation alone. Ranked after municipalities, as Arizona's and Nevada's are, so they are drawn above the larger areas around them, and before the San Francisco layers, none of which this land touches. Drawn although no district is drawn on most of this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — California has 150 such areas, held by 98 nations: 94 seated in California, one (the Colorado River Indian Tribes) in Arizona, one (the Washoe Tribe) in Nevada, and two (the Round Valley Indian Tribes and the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation) for which the Bureau lists no office town, given the town their own sites give.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: The council of each nation whose own page names the whole of it, 49 of the 98 nations, re-read weekly by scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py into data/app/tribal-councils.json and named with the date each was read. Every other card says why it names nobody, in words measured nation by nation on 2026-11-13 (ROSTER_BLOCKED in scripts/build_tribal_areas.py): a site that refused this project or could not be read, a page naming part of a council or none of it, or no site of the nation's own. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json), which lists neither a city nor a state for two of these nations, the Round Valley Indian Tribes and the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation; for both the seat is the town the nation's own site gives, read 2026-11-12, and the card says so. The Capitan Grande Reservation is shared by the Capitan Grande Band's two groups, Barona and Viejas, and its card lists both with their seats and sites. The Bureau lists no website for 28 of the nations, among them the Fort Mojave Indian Tribe, the Quechan Tribe and the Colorado River Indian Tribes; the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: California — the 150 pieces of land above, which reach into 34 of its 58 counties. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land the Census draws for a government.

source.answers: For the picked contest, the choice with the most votes in each San Francisco precinct, and on the card the clicked precinct's votes for every contest on its ballot, from governor to its Assembly, Senate, BART and Supervisor seats, the judges and the state and city measures, and the contest's total across the city. Preliminary until the Department of Elections certifies the count, and the card and the map key say so.

boundary.label: Voting precincts published by the Department of Elections on DataSF (jg6x-23ig), the same outlines Election Precinct draws

source.people: The candidates and their votes come from the San Francisco Department of Elections' preliminary Statement of the Vote by precinct for the 3 November 2026 election, the Excel workbook its detailed reports page links, read daily by ca/scripts/sf_election_results_scraper.py. In a ranked-choice contest (the Supervisors, Assessor-Recorder and Public Defender) the counts are first choices. Write-in votes are left out, as the Department's own totals leave them out. Candidates are ordered alphabetically by name as printed, with Yes before No on a measure; colours follow that order, never a party.
source.applies: San Francisco. The statewide offices, judges and propositions, and the House, Senate and Assembly districts that cross the city line, reach beyond it, so their totals on the card are the city's part of the contest.

layer_count_note: Thread-5: legislative chambers now pre-built SF-clipped geometry (data/app); supervisor-district is a bespoke roster-joined registerLayer; 11 layers total; + 3 amenity nearest-point layers (post-office, library, early-voting) = 14; + bart-director + election-precinct (parity-debt closures, 2026-07) = 16; + election-results (2026-11) = 17; + county, municipality and the three school district tilings when the app grew to the whole state (2026-11) = 22; + tribal-government (2026-11-12) = 23

negative_point.note: The Mexicali Valley in Mexico, about 15 km south of the border at Calexico — outside California and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-11 against TIGERweb's state layer (controls: San Francisco City Hall returns California, and Mexicali, Baja California, returns no state). IT IS IN ANOTHER COUNTRY, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: San Francisco's outline (ca/scripts/build_sf_county_outline.py, the union of the eleven shipped supervisor districts). The coverage test of every layer built from the city's own data (inSanFrancisco), so those layers hide outside the city, and the Data gaps panel's test for which gaps apply where the reader clicked.

The state outline (ca/scripts/build_state_outline.py, the dissolve of the state's 58 counties): the lighter band of the coverage wash, the statewide officials line's ground, and the ZIP layer's coverage test.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside ca-state-outline.json, the ground the ZIP layer's coverage test (inCalifornia) answers on; --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

California's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — 103 reservations and rancherias and 47 pieces of off-reservation trust land, held by 98 nations, five pieces drawn whole across the state line, at the Census's own detail (1.12 MB, 258 KB gzipped, under Arizona's simplified 1.44 MB). The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-11-12; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

rosters.note: The councils of the nations whose own page names the whole of it, keyed by the Census AIANNH code of each piece of land — scripts/build_tribal_areas.py --rosters from data/tribal-councils.json, which scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py re-reads weekly (update-tribal-councils.yml, listed in the Wisconsin worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance). Merged onto tribal-areas.json by the layer's loader, so the land stays cache-first and the names network-first.

The officers California elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from ca/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.

San Francisco's election results by precinct: the index (groups, precinct keys, the part file each precinct is in, and per contest its choices, totals and its leader string, trimmed to the run of precincts it is on the ballot in); each precinct's own counts sit in election-results/p<first two digits>.json, fetched on a click and never cached by the worker. From the Department of Elections' Statement of the Vote by ca/scripts/sf_election_results_scraper.py + build_sf_election_results.py through scripts/election_results_common.py, checked daily by ca-update-election-results.yml; certified stays false until the Department certifies the results. Network-first: the count can change.

Known data gaps keyed by gap id, driving the Data gaps panel — emitted from the fleet guidebook's GUIDEBOOK:BEGIN gaps block by scripts/build_coverage_gaps.py, which reads this fork's this_metro key (--check is the drift gate). Network-first like the rosters: a closed gap should stop being advertised on the next visit. WENT 3 TO 2 ON 2026-09-19 when `sf-congress-district-offices` was RETIRED as false — the card renders the district office and 50 of 52 records carry one, measured in Chromium. That is the only reason this number ever moves down: a gap CLOSED on a measurement, which is what the sentence above anticipates. It is never lowered to get past a build that emptied the file, which is the collapse this floor exists to catch — if it fails and no gap was deliberately retired, fix the build. And it is edited HERE, never in the generated region: hand-editing ca/scripts/validate_index.py is what turned this change's first CI run red.
CA U.S. House reps (52 seats; vacancies allowed) - unitedstates/congress-legislators
SF Board of Supervisors (11) - DataSF hcgx-vtsb sup_name

GeoJSON FeatureCollection (type/metadata/features - key floor is shape-only); hand-curated per election from sf.gov Dept of Elections pages, network-first so a new election's list is never served stale
9 BART directors keyed by district, hand-verified against bart.gov/about/bod (staggered 4-year terms; re-verify after each even-year November - see WATCH.md)
